$comment: Idioms derived from Gordon Reid's Synth Secrets, which is the one source in
this library's reading list that we can actually open: 63 articles for Sound
On Sound, mirrored as markdown, fetched into a gitignored `.corpus/` by
corpus.py. Every record here carries `provenance: read` and an `anchor`
quoting the article, and provenance_check.py demotes any of them whose quote
turns out not to be there.
THE REST OF THE LIBRARY IS `canon`, AND THAT IS NOT A LESSER LABEL. Strange,
Patch & Tweak, Welsh, the Buchla and Serge manuals and Elsea are in
copyright and not openly published; the original ARP 2600 owner's manual and
the 2600 Patch Book ARE openly published by Korg and are page scans with no
text layer, so 111 pages of worked patches yield nothing a checker could
read. Nothing citing any of them can honestly be `read`, and this file does
The technique is derived; the words are ours. An anchor quotes the article
so the citation can be falsified, not so the article can be reproduced --
the copyright is Sound On Sound's and Gordon Reid's, and a phrase long
enough to identify a passage is the whole of what is kept.

implies: timbre that changes as you play up the keyboard
idioms.is: Amplitude modulation with the modulator held at one frequency while the carrier is played, so the sum and difference tones land at different intervals for every note and the timbre changes across the keyboard.
idioms.sounds_right_when: low notes sound almost consonant and higher ones progressively more clangorous — the same patch, a different sound at every pitch.
idioms.source: Synth Secrets, Part 11: Amplitude Modulation — the fixed-modulator cases

anchor.quote: fixed-Modulator AM is most useful for creating aggressive and conventionally 'unmusical' sounds that change dramatically as you play up and down the keyboard

axis.position: the modulator stands still while the carrier is played
axis.set_by: whether the playing voltage is split to the modulator as well — the one thing on this axis that IS a cable, which is why both positions can be checked
axis.$comment: Two ways to patch one technique, with opposite musical consequences. Held still, the modulator makes the interval between the sum and difference tones a fixed number of hertz, so their RATIO to the carrier changes with every note and the timbre travels. Tracked, the ratio is constant and the timbre is not.

topology.describe: the carrier has to pass through the amplifier
a second oscillator has to modulate that amplifier's gain at audio rate — below hearing this is tremolo, and the sidebands never appear
the carrier has to be played, or there is no range across which the timbre can change

listen_for.sounds_like: a metallic tone whose character will not hold still as you move up the keyboard: consonant in one register, harsh and bell-like a fifth higher, with no knob having moved
listen_for.confusable_with: the tracking version, which produces the same kind of tone but keeps it constant across the range. NOTHING HERE RULES THAT OUT: the difference is whether one playing voltage reaches both oscillators, and a requirement names the roles at the two ends of one cable — it cannot say 'and no OTHER cable carries this same voltage somewhere else'. So a tracking patch satisfies this idiom too, and only a listener can separate them: play an octave and hear whether the character survives the move.

expect.why: the sum and difference tones are enharmonic for most carrier pitches, so a pitch tracker should lose its grip for part of the run

common_mistakes.message: nothing modulates the amplifier at audio rate, so there are no sum and difference tones
no carrier passes through the amplifier
nothing plays the carrier, so the changing-across-the-keyboard effect never happens

implies: inharmonic timbre that plays in tune
idioms.is: Amplitude modulation with the playing voltage split so that carrier and modulator move together, so the sum and difference tones keep a constant ratio to the carrier and one inharmonic timbre transposes across the keyboard.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the sound is clangorous and yet plays like an instrument — the same character at every pitch.
idioms.source: Synth Secrets, Part 11: Amplitude Modulation — the tracking-modulator case

anchor.quote: the relationships between the Difference, Carrier and Sum remain constant if both the Carrier and the Modulator track the keyboard equally

axis.position: the modulator is played alongside the carrier
axis.set_by: whether the playing voltage is split to the modulator as well — the one thing on this axis that IS a cable, which is why both positions can be checked
axis.$comment: The split is the whole difference. Tracked, the sidebands sit at fixed percentages of the carrier and the timbre transposes; held still, they do not and it does not.

topology.describe: the playing voltage has to be split, because it has to reach two oscillators
the modulator has to be played by the SAME voltage — that is what keeps the sidebands at a constant ratio to the carrier
the carrier has to pass through the amplifier

listen_for.sounds_like: a bell or gong that can be played as an instrument: unmistakably inharmonic, and identical in character whether you play it low or high
listen_for.confusable_with: the fixed-modulator version, which changes character across the range; the test is to play an octave and hear whether the timbre survives the move

common_mistakes.message: the modulator is not played, so the timbre changes with every note instead of transposing
the playing voltage is never split, so it cannot reach both oscillators
no carrier passes through the amplifier

implies: rasp at the start of a note
idioms.is: A fast modulator sent to the filter through an amplifier that a short envelope opens, so the note begins unstable and settles — the roughness lasts only as long as the attack, not the note.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the note starts with a rasp and cleans up; holding the note gives you a steady tone, not a permanent buzz.
idioms.source: Synth Secrets, Part 25: Synthesizing Brass Instruments — the growl patch

anchor.quote: we patch the modulation into the filter through a VCA whose gain is controlled by an AD contour generator

topology.describe: the modulator has to pass through an amplifier — that amplifier is what makes the growl temporary
a short envelope has to open it, or the growl runs for the whole note and the patch buzzes
the gated modulation goes to the FILTER, not to the oscillator — on the oscillator the same cable is frequency modulation, which produces sidebands and destroys the timbre instead of roughening it

listen_for.sounds_like: the catch at the front of a blown note, gone within a fraction of a second: a real brass note takes about a dozen cycles to settle, which is roughly fifty milliseconds at middle C, and the growl should not outlast that by much
listen_for.confusable_with: vibrato on the oscillator, which moves the pitch and lasts; this moves only the colour and stops

expect.why: the growl has to move the brightness measurably, but only briefly — a modulator around 80Hz is what the source recommends, which is far above the 25Hz ceiling many LFOs stop at

common_mistakes.message: nothing gates the growl, so it buzzes for the whole note instead of only the attack
no modulator passes through the amplifier
the gated modulation never reaches the filter

implies: make it sound like a wooden instrument
idioms.is: Several band-pass filters in parallel, summed, tuned to fixed frequencies that do not follow the note — the resonances of an instrument's body, which stay where they are however high you play.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the sound has a consistent character across the range, with certain notes ringing more than their neighbours.
idioms.source: Synth Secrets, Part 49: Practical Bowed-string Synthesis — the violin body-resonance filter bank

anchor.quote: we will set the first two filters to accentuate the body resonances at 300Hz and 700Hz

axis.position: tuned to an instrument body's resonances
axis.set_by: where the filters are tuned and how sharp they are — knobs, so the patch that makes a violin body and the patch that makes a vowel are the same cables
axis.$comment: A bank of parallel band-pass filters summed. Tuned to 300Hz, 700Hz and a broad peak around 3kHz it reads as a bowed string; tuned to the vowel formants it reads as a voice. One structure, and the tuning is what a checker cannot see.

topology.describe: a harmonically rich source has to reach the filters
the bands have to be summed — in PARALLEL, so their peaks add; in series they would multiply and narrow to one band, which is a different technique

listen_for.sounds_like: a body rather than a filter: the emphasis stays at the same absolute frequencies as you play up and down, so some notes bloom and others sit back, exactly as an acoustic instrument does
listen_for.confusable_with: a filter that tracks the keyboard, where every note has identical colour — the giveaway is whether the uneven-ness across the range survives transposition

expect.why: fixed resonances do not sweep; a large brightness variation over a sustained note means something is modulating the bank, which this technique does not do

common_mistakes.message: the bands are never summed, so only one resonance is heard

idioms.is: A lagged pitch voltage passed through a quantizer, so the glide between two notes is travelled in steps rather than smoothly — a run up the scale instead of a slide.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you hear individual semitones going past on the way to the destination.
idioms.source: Synth Secrets, Part 16: From Sample & Hold To Sample-rate Converters — the quantiser applied to a continuously changing CV

anchor.quote: convert a continuously rising or falling CV into a 'stepped' one -- an effect that we often use to convert portamento into glissando

topology.describe: the pitch voltage has to be lagged first — with nothing to smooth, the quantizer has nothing to step through
the LAGGED voltage has to reach the quantizer, in that order; quantizing first and lagging afterwards smooths the steps back out
the stepped voltage has to play the oscillator

listen_for.sounds_like: a harpist's run rather than a trombone's slide: the same journey between two notes, taken in audible steps, and the number of steps depends on how long the lag takes
listen_for.confusable_with: portamento, which is the same patch without the quantizer and slides continuously

expect.why: a glissando that passes through fewer than three pitches is a portamento with a rounding error

common_mistakes.message: the lagged voltage never reaches the quantizer, so this is an ordinary portamento
nothing lags the pitch, so there is no journey for the quantizer to step through
the stepped voltage never reaches a pitch input
